name: Meter
description: A graphical display of a numeric value within a defined range, such as battery percentage or fuel level. Not for progress indication.

roles.description: Identifies the element as a meter

optional_attributes.description: Human-readable value string when numeric alone is insufficient

notes: <meter> = a measurement within a known range (disk usage, score). <progress> = how far a task has got. They are not interchangeable.
Neither is a form control and neither is focusable — do not put tabindex on them.
Screen reader support for role='meter' has historically been patchy. ALWAYS render the value as visible text next to it; do not rely on the element alone to convey it.
aria-valuenow/min/max are only needed on a div-built meter. <meter> derives them from value/min/max.
aria-valuetext when the raw number is not meaningful: aria-valuenow='2' aria-valuetext='Medium'.
A meter is never interactive. If the user can change the value it is a slider (patterns/slider.md).
<progress> with no value attribute is INDETERMINATE (a spinner) — omitting value by accident is a real bug.
native_element: <meter> for a measurement in a range; <progress> for task completion

raweb_criteria.reason: The value must be exposed. Screen reader support for role='meter' is uneven, so a visible text value is not optional.
A gauge that only changes colour (green/amber/red) conveys its state by colour alone — add a text value.
The text value must meet contrast against its background.
